ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Geldwäschegesetz (GwG) of 23 June 2017, as last amended; § 20 GwG (definition of beneficial owner); § 21 GwG (notification duty to the Transparenzregister); §§ 3 and 12 GwG (customer due diligence and enforcement); Transparenzregister- und Finanzinformationengesetz (TraFinG); combined with GmbHG § 8(1)(3) as regards the shareholder declaration in notarized incorporation filings.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the UBO's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / excerpt from commercial register of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry authority of the foreign parent company's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ownership structure chart identifying all natural-person beneficial owners holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of shares or voting rights
Bank reference letter or source of funds declaration for the initial contribution to the GmbH share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or certified translation as required by the German notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: English translation of foreign public documents, certified by a German sworn translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translation office admitted in Germany
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only where the document originates from a non-Hague-Apostille state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against German domestic sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, and politically exposed persons (PEP) databases. Screening is required before Notar appointment and before any share capital transfer. In relation to a food-and-beverage franchise, the franchisee, its directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners must be screened. Negative-match records, source-of-funds evidence, and UBO declarations must be retained for at least five years in accordance with GwG § 8 and § 9.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Unternehmensregister (www.unternehmensregister.de), with actual name clearance performed at the registry section (Registerabteilung) of the competent Amtsgericht responsible for the future registered seat, coordinated through the notary using the Land register portal / common register portal of the German Länder.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin script and be electronically reproducible in the German Handelsregister. Names containing non-Latin scripts or non-standard special characters are not accepted; transliteration into a German-recognized Latin form is required. The name must not conflict with existing registered names or require misleading indication of legal form; 'GmbH' must appear in the name in accepted German form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Amtsgericht refuses a proposed name, the notary or incorporator may address the refusal by filing an administrative appeal (Erinnerung) to the competent Amtsgericht within two weeks, followed by an immediate complaint (Beschwerde) to the Higher Regional Court (Oberlandesgericht) if the Amtsgericht does not cure the defect. The appeal must be filed through a German attorney in the form required by each Land's judicial procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the registered seat for a GmbH. Under GmbHG § 4a, the registered seat must be a fixed, actual place maintainable as the company's administrative base. A post-box or pure virtual correspondence address is insufficient for registration; a physical registered office in Germany with actual access and reasonable service capacity is required. A virtual office may only serve as a supplemental correspondence address and does not satisfy commercial substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months by the local trade authority (Gewerbeaufsicht), tax office, or, in case of AML triggers, by the competent Financial Intelligence Unit or customs enforcement; the risk increases to moderate if the registered office is unusually shared or has no observable business operations.

English certified translation of German registration documents and apostilled foreign due diligence documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gesetz betreffend die Gesellschaften mit beschränkter Haftung (GmbH-Gesetz, GmbHG), particularly §§1, 5, 7, 8, 10, 35-38, 46
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) and Application for Registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is €25,000; at least €12,500 (50%) must be paid in cash before registration. The capital must be deposited in a German bank account and confirmed by the bank (Bankbescheinigung). For single-member GmbH, the shareholder must provide security for any unpaid capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Association as presented are adopted and the company is established as a Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung (GmbH) under German law. RESOLVED, that the share capital of €25,000 is subscribed as follows: [Shareholder names and amounts]. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [Address]. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Managing Director (Geschäftsführer) with sole authority to represent the company. RESOLVED, that the Managing Director is authorized to execute all documents and file all applications necessary to register the company with the Commercial Register and obtain all required licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) and schedule a notarization appointment. All shareholders must appear before the notary with valid identification. The notary will read the articles, verify legal capacity, and execute the notarial deed. The notary will then forward the deed to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each shareholder
Power of attorney if a representative acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies, correct the documents and reschedule the appointment. Additional fees may apply for re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: German bank (e.g., Commerzbank, Deutsche Bank, or local Sparkasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the GmbH (in formation). Deposit at least €12,500 (half of the minimum capital) into the account. Obtain a Bankbescheinigung (bank confirmation) stating that the funds are at the free disposal of the managing director. This confirmation is required for registration.
required_dossiers: Valid ID of the managing director
Proof of address of the company (if available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application, provide additional due diligence documents (e.g., source of funds) or choose another bank. The deposit must be made in EUR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Registration with the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration (Anmeldung) to the local court. The application must be signed by all managing directors and include the notarized articles, bank confirmation, list of managing directors with their signatures, and a declaration of compliance with capital requirements. The court reviews the documents and issues the registration entry.
required_dossiers: List of managing directors with specimen signatures
Application form (Anmeldung) signed by managing directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court raises objections, respond within 10 days with clarifications or amended documents. If the application is rejected, correct the issues and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the commercial register entry, register the company with the local tax office. Submit the registration form (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung) online or in person. The tax office will issue a tax number (Steuernummer) and, if applicable, a VAT identification number (USt-IdNr.). This is required for invoicing and tax compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, provide it promptly. If the application is delayed, follow up with the tax office and ensure all required documents are submitted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Trade Office (Gewerbeamt) and Food Safety Authority (Lebensmittelüberwachungsamt)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gewerbeanmeldung (Business Registration) and Food Business Operation Permit (Lebensmittelbetriebserlaubnis)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Environment Agency (Umweltbundesamt) and Local Environmental Authority (Untere Umweltschutzbehörde)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category II) – no full EIA required for small-scale beverage production and franchise operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with local municipal sewer regulations (Abwassersatzung); VOC emissions from syrup production must meet TA-Luft limits; waste handling per Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz (Circular Economy Act).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire department (Feuerwehr) for premises; structural load inspection from building authority (Bauamt) for any modifications; workplace safety clearance from occupational health and safety authority (Gewerbeaufsichtsamt) including hygiene training for food handlers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Bundesministerium der Finanzen (BMF) / Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt) / local Finanzamt; official portals ELSTER (www.elster.de) and BZSt (www.bzst.de)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic GmbH: after notarisation and Handelsregister entry, the local Finanzamt assigns the Steuernummer automatically; within 4 weeks of formation the managing director files the electronic 'Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung' in ELSTER. For VAT cross-border operations, apply to BZSt (ELSTER/Formular USt 1 TU) for the USt-IdNr. For a foreign entity with a German permanent establishment, registration is made with the local Finanzamt (place of German establishment) to obtain a Steuernummer and a USt-IdNr. from BZSt; foreign entities without a permanent establishment may still be required to register for German VAT and may be granted an USt-IdNr. after demonstrating taxable activity (e.g. purchase/sales invoices, contracts, IHK confirmation).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election. A GmbH is always subject to entity-level corporation tax (15% plus 5.5% solidarity surcharge) and trade tax; no pass-through treatment. Available elections: (i) Organschaft (fiscal unity) for corporate income tax/trade tax/VAT with German subsidiaries under a domination and profit-and-loss transfer agreement (§14, 17, 18 KStG; §2(2) Nr.2 UStG); (ii) optional application of the §19 UStG small-business VAT exemption if turnover thresholds (€25,000/€100,000) are met; (iii) for partnerships only, option to be taxed as a corporation under §1a KStG, not applicable to a GmbH; hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD) are mandatory, not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No absolute registration threshold; any entrepreneur making taxable supplies in Germany must register for VAT. The §19 UStG small-business exemption (elective) applies only if prior-year turnover did not exceed €25,000 and current-year expected turnover does not exceed €100,000; a GmbH carrying on franchise licensing and syrup supply will normally exceed these limits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Structured electronic invoicing (CEN EN 16931 / XRechnung / ZUGFeRD) is mandatory for German B2B transactions: from 1 Jan 2025 every entrepreneur must be able to receive e-invoices; from 1 Jan 2026 entrepreneurs with prior-year turnover > €800,000 must issue e-invoices; from 1 Jan 2027 all entrepreneurs must issue e-invoices. No central real-time fiscal clearance platform or digital stamping exists for VAT; e-invoices are exchanged directly. VAT returns, EC Sales Lists and Intrastat are filed via ELSTER; customs exports are cleared electronically in real time by German Customs (ATLAS/AES).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Germany to a non-EU destination are zero-rated under §4 No.1 letter a and §6 UStG if the goods physically leave the EU and the supplier holds the export proof (Ausfuhrnachweis). Intra-EU supplies of goods (e.g. syrups, equipment) to franchisees are exempt under §6a UStG when the customer is a taxable dealer identified by a valid USt-IdNr. and the goods are dispatched to another EU Member State. Franchise royalties and licensing fees received from foreign franchisees are treated as B2B services supplied at the recipient's establishment under §3a(2) UStG; the supply is outside the scope of German VAT (reverse charge on the customer). The supplier must keep transport and payment documents showing that the goods left Germany/the EU and that the remuneration was received.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung) validated in ATLAS with exit confirmation (Ausgangsvermerk)
Bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or postal/courier dispatch proof
Commercial invoice, export order and sales contract
Inward remittance certificate or bank payment confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Finanzamt reviews export documentation during tax audits (Betriebsprüfung), including retrospective verification of the export evidence and the payment. Deficient or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract reassessment of VAT at 19%, monthly late surcharges (Säumniszuschlag of 1% p.m.), default interest at 6% p.a., and penalty fines; negligent tax shortfall (§378 AO) up to €50,000; intentional tax evasion (§370 AO) may lead to up to 10 years' imprisonment plus confiscation; the VAT assessment limitation period is extended to 10 years for tax evasion, allowing retrospective clawbacks for that full period. Managing directors can become personally liable under §69 AO for lost taxes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Deutsche Bundesbank (the German Central Bank), exercising responsibilities under the German Foreign Trade and Payments Ordinance (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung – AWV) and the European System of Central Banks; the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) supplements the prudential framework for banks and payment institutions. The Bundesbank operates the public statistics and reporting mechanism for cross-border payments but does not administer exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Germany for both current-account and capital-account transactions. European Union free-movement-of-capital rules and German national law impose no foreign-exchange licenses, no convertibility restrictions, and no special profit-remittance approvals. A German GmbH may remit dividends to foreign shareholders by an ordinary distribution after a formal shareholder dividend resolution, preparation of annual financial statements, and the satisfaction of German corporate law requirements; the only friction points are the 26.375% withholding tax (including solidarity surcharge) that generally applies under the Internal Revenue Act (Einkommensteuergesetz) unless a treaty exemption/relief is obtained, the need to comply with annual statutory audits if applicable, and the prohibition on distributions that would impair share capital under the GmbHG.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds in Germany. The resident GmbH may retain foreign-currency receipts abroad or convert them freely. The compliance requirement is statistical reporting to the Deutsche Bundesbank: all cross-border payments exceeding EUR 12,500, including export and import payment transactions, must be reported within five calendar days using the AWV reporting channels (usually electronically through the Bundesbank's external-statistics portal). The reporting obligation captures amounts, currency, counterparty jurisdiction, and the national payment-purpose classification; it is not an exchange-control authorisation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional / Medium-Low. An offshore digital electronic-money institution must be either an EU/EEA licensed e-money institution passporting under PSD2, or a BaFin-licensed German e-money institution; regulatory 'EU passport' notification to BaFin is possible for EU/EEA EMIs. A third-country EMI with no legal presence in Germany may not freely hold operational treasury accounts for the GmbH. The practical constraints are limitations on account balances, absence of deposit guarantee, sanctions- and AML-risk management, KYC acceptance for corporate customers, and lower access to intraday liquidity, trade finance, and SWIFT-based clearing needed for franchise trade flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance of all directors is not a universal statutory requirement. Under the German Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) a bank may identify the individual signatories through permitted remote video identification (VideoIdent) or the eID function of a government-issued identity card. However, for a GmbH with foreign beneficial owners, franchise royalty concentration, and cross-border payments, most Tier-1 banks will require at least one managing director or an authorised German-resident agent to complete a physical or high-grade video interview before accepting the business. The bank must verify the managing director's identity, authority to represent, UBO registry extraction (§ 20 GwG), and commercial rationale; documentary evidence must correspond in German or be accompanied by certified translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Registergericht (commercial register) lists a recently incorporated GmbH whose sole shareholder is a non-EU entity or individual, raising private-investment-company and conduit-entity concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified articles of association, current excerpt from the Handelsregister, transparent chain-of-ownership chart, Ultimate Beneficial Owner declaration pursuant to the Transparency Register, source-of-wealth evidence for the shareholder, annual tax residence certificates, and a business plan showing the franchise master licence, or sub-licences, operational premises, and employment substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The franchise licensing model creates frequent, relatively high-volume royalty receipts from multiple EEA and third-country franchisees, triggering suspicious-transaction-risk flags around layering or disguised payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master franchise and unit franchise agreements, royalty calculation worksheets tied to audited POS data, sample franchisee invoices and bank statements, group transfer-pricing documentation (OECD Chapter VI compliant), VAT/Intrastat filings, and a named compliance officer / AML contact accountable under GwG.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments for imported boba raw materials, packaging, and equipment originate from Hong Kong, Taiwan, or mainland Chinese suppliers, and the bank observes swifter trade-related outflow patterns equitable to the GmbH's capital base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial purchase contracts and LC/collection documents, bills of lading, customs entry summaries, commercial invoices and packing lists, and, where necessary, a capped monthly disbursement schedule aligned with documented inventory purchases and verified by an initial due-diligence meeting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The preferred protocol is a euro-denominated SWIFT MT103/MT202 settlement into the GmbH's German operational or capital escrow account. The sender must use the cross-border payment purpose code corresponding to the acquisition of an equity interest in a German limited-liability company (under the Bundesbank AWV reporting classification, category for inbound direct investment/participation), and the commercial register entry should be contemporaneously updated to evidence the capital increase or contribution. The remittance must be accompanied by a transfer documentation package containing the bank's foreign-exchange/AML departure declaration, the tax clearance if applicable, and, for payments exceeding EUR 12,500, the Bundesbank AWV report. The German receiving bank will request the same AWV classification and may freeze the funds until the source of funds and the underlying legitimate ownership are reconciled.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Franchise royalty outpayments and trade purchases should be executed over SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA jurisdictions or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro payments within the SEPA zone. Bulk commodity purchases (raw tapioca pearls, tea leaves, syrups, disposable cups, sealing films) to East Asian suppliers should be routed through documentary commercial letters of credit (irrevocable, confirmed where appropriate) or documentary collections when the supplier risk is material. For recurring interoperable payments with franchisees, use ISO 20022-enhanced straight-through-processing messages, each carrying the appropriate creditor reference and AWV reporting classification if above the statutory threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNY outright FX forwards with a licensed German or EU banking counterparty, restricted to hedging forecast Boba-Tea franchise payments and goods procurement invoices.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY or TWD insofar as a permissible liquidity and trade-forecast exposure exists and the bank has a master agreement under the ISDA or German Rahmenvertrag für Finanztermingeschäfte.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/CNY and EUR/USD) used for interest-rate/currency alignment on long-term operating or lease liabilities.

Exchange-traded and OTC FX options, but only with a physical settlement and underlying commercial exposure; speculative or transparently speculative derivatives are not permissible under German MaRisk-consistent treasury policies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresabschluss) including balance sheet, profit and loss account and notes, approved by the shareholders' meeting and published electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Electronic Federal Gazette (Bundesanzeiger), operated by Bundesanzeiger Verlag; disclosure mirrored to the Commercial Register (Handelsregister, local Amtsgericht)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preparation within 8 months after fiscal-year end for small GmbHs (3 months for medium/large companies, §264 HGB); publication with the Bundesanzeiger within 12 months of the balance-sheet date (§325 HGB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fine (Zwangsgeld) of EUR 2,500–25,000 per omission under §335 HGB; regulatory fines up to EUR 50,000 under §334 HGB; after five consecutive years of non-disclosure, ex officio strike-off from the Handelsregister pursuant to §§394–397 FamFG commences

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Körperschaftsteuererklärung 2024) with profit determination schedule and supporting accounting records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax office (Finanzamt) competent for the DE_GMBH registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 31 of the year following the assessment year; automatically extended to February 28/29 of the second following year where the return is prepared by a licensed tax adviser (Steuerberater) (§149 AO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge under §152 AO up to EUR 25,000 (0.25% of the assessed corporate tax per commenced month, minimum EUR 25 per month); late-payment interest at 0.15% per month (1.8% p.a.) under §233a AO; estimated assessment under §162 AO if accounts are withheld

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Trade tax return (Gewerbesteuererklärung 2024) covering trade earnings of the franchise operation and syrup supply chain
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax office (Finanzamt) collecting for the municipality that sets the trade-tax multiplier (Hebesatz)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 31 of the following assessment year; extended to February 28/29 of the second following year where prepared by a professional tax adviser (§149 AO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge up to EUR 25,000 (0.25% per commenced month); late-payment interest at 0.15% per month (1.8% p.a.) under §233a AO; municipal enforcement follows the trade-tax assessment notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value added tax return (Umsatzsteuererklärung 2024) reconciling monthly/quarterly advance returns for franchise royalties, local POS sales and cross-border EU supplies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax office (Finanzamt) competent for the DE_GMBH registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 31 of the following calendar year; the administrative grace period extends the deadline to December 31 of the following calendar year when the return is filed by a tax adviser (§149 AO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge up to EUR 25,000 under §152 AO; late-payment interest at 0.15% per month (1.8% p.a.); estimated assessment against rejected VAT refund positions may follow

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Transparency Register notification of beneficial owners (Transparenzregister / Mitteilung nach §20 GwG) covering the DE_GMBH shareholding structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Transparency Register (Transparenzregister) filed electronically through the Bundesanzeiger publishing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: initial notification within one month of incorporation or a qualifying shareholding change; updated notification must be made immediately (unverzüglich) upon any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership (§20 GwG); no separate calendar-year confirmation filing exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 100,000 per violation (up to EUR 1,000,000 for serious or repeated infringements) under §§56–57 GwG; violations may additionally obstruct future capital-distribution declarations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit under §§316–317 HGB is mandatory where the GmbH exceeds two of the three thresholds in §267 HGB for three consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total > EUR 6.0m, annual turnover > EUR 12.0m, average workforce > 50 employees; medium/large size is triggered at EUR 20.0m, EUR 40.0m and 250 employees. Small GmbHs below these thresholds are statutorily exempt from the mandatory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: German GAAP under the Commercial Code (HGB) as amended by BilRUG 2015, including the Grundsätze ordnungsmäßiger Buchführung (GoB); tax accounts follow the authoritative principle (Maßgeblichkeitsgrundsatz, §5 EStG); IFRS may be elected voluntarily for publication per §325(2a) HGB while HGB accounts remain legally determinative for shareholder distributions. Retention rule: 10 years for books of account and annual financial statements and 6 years for commercial correspondence (§257 HGB, §147 AO); the schema field value 7 is retained as a rounded template constant.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Germany applies a continuous, event-driven transparency obligation rather than a single annual confirmation: the DE_GMBH must report all beneficial owners to the Transparenzregister within one month of formation (§20 GwG) and must file an updated notification immediately upon any share transfer, change of control or correction of register data; shareholder-list (Gesellschafterliste) mutations filed with the Handelsregister are mirrored to the Transparenzregister electronically. The register must be accurate as at each fiscal-year end; no separate year-end UBO declaration is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Gesellschafterliste) — maintained by the managing directors at the registered office and resubmitted to the Handelsregister upon any membership change (§40 GmbHG)
Register of Managing Directors and Authorised Officers — current directory of directors filed with the Handelsregister (§39 GmbHG) and kept available for inspection
Shareholder Resolution Minute Book (Niederschriften) — minutes of all shareholders' meetings and consents in lieu of meetings, retained on site for at least 10 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 2,300 per annum (EUR 1,100 – 2,100) for registered-office provision, statutory correspondence handling, Handelsregister filings and secretarial administration by a German corporate-services provider or tax adviser
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – 19,500 (EUR 5,000 – 18,000) for a full statutory audit by a certified auditor (Wirtschaftsprüfer) where the HGB size thresholds are met; for a small exempt GmbH, an optional voluntary review typically costs USD 1,100 – 3,800 (EUR 1,000 – 3,500)

stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the tax number assigned by the local Finanzamt upon incorporation.
